correctness.rationale: The four coefficient coordinates are independent as functions on the two halves and satisfy UV=WX exactly for nonzero rank-one coefficients. A proper zero fiber is given by eta=-V/U or eta=-X/W, and a whole-half mask forces a single surviving coordinate. For specified proper fibers alpha,beta on both halves, normalizing U=1 forces V=-alpha, X=-beta W and W²=alpha/beta, giving exactly the claimed two classes and the reflection sign change. With just one specified fiber the other ratio avoids a finite set. For the empty fiber, the displayed one-parameter family is a witness, not the entire fiber: in the all-nonzero stratum both ratios must avoid eta(A), and in the product-zero stratum each half has exactly one nonzero coefficient. Thus the claimed cardinalities, all boundary cases L=2 and the support sizes follow. Direct Schur orthogonality for the stated transform gives the block vuᵀ/2 and no others. The attached verification note and script were inspected; the finite, recorded checks were not executed and are not needed for the symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: The distinct indexed spinor theorem is exact coverage through a projective central quotient and pullback, not merely an analogy. Let D=diag(lambda,lambda^-1), lambda=exp(pi i/L), J=i rho_chi(s). They generate Dic_L with center ±I, quotient D_L and J²=-I. If eta(a)=lambda^(2j), rho_chi(a) is a nonzero scalar multiple of D^j, and rho_chi(as) of D^j J. The map a→j, s→reflection is onto D_L. Thus fixed-representation projective coefficients and their masks on G and Dic_L correspond by the same (u,v), pointwise nonzero rescalings and pullbacks from the quotient for the masks. Specifically, a coefficient is determined by one choice of representative in each projective group fiber, up to those prescribed rescalings; the identification respects overall scalars in both directions. Each antipodal pair induces precisely one H-coset in a half. Cosets of <D> give the two whole halves; every nonrotation maximal cyclic subgroup is generated by an outside element with square -I and has order four, and its cosets give exactly all pairs of one quotient point from each half. This also holds for Q8, where the designated rotation subgroup is one of three order-four subgroups. Hence the indexed theorem transports all masks, multiplicities, ranks, counts and spatial-support sizes, with mask sizes on G scaled by |H| relative to the quotient. This establishes coverage, not priority within the same date.
